items_missed: No "How are you today?" check-in at the open
No explicit agenda statement (gather details, then walk through pricing, ~10-15 min) before diving into questions
No explicit "Sound good?" confirmation of the agenda
Didn't probe narrow hallways/tight turns specifically (only surfaced low-hanging tree via a parking question)
Never asked if she needs packing services
Never asked the open-ended stressor question ("anything you're particularly worried about?")
Estimate walkthrough didn't cover walk distance or use an equivalents reference (e.g. school bus comparison)
Traffic not addressed as a time variable
No "Does that make sense?" close after the Save Your Ass prep speech
Never stated business hours or how to reach the branch
Gave inconsistent mover counts for the same estimate (said "two movers" then later "four movers") which muddies the quote
No laughter or deeper rapport moment beyond a brief weather aside
No mention of the 60 cents/lb baseline valuation as the insurance alternative to No Worries coverage
top_strength: Handled a genuinely complex move (patio-furniture side stop, two storage units, seven measured artworks, multiple fragile/solid-wood pieces) with careful itemization and proactively recalculated the estimate downward twice in real time as the customer changed scope, keeping cost transparent throughout.
coaching_note: Skipped the agenda-statement opener and jumped straight into detail-gathering, and later gave conflicting mover counts (two movers, then four) for the same job — tighten the open with a clear agenda/sound-good check and double back to confirm a single consistent crew size before quoting the final number.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently polite and patient through a long, detail-heavy call, but heavy "mm-hmm" filler, garbled phrasing, and the mover-count mix-up kept it feeling transactional rather than warm.
